question.text: In a potentiometer arrangement, a cell of emf <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> gives a balance point at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length of wire. This cell is now replaced by another cell of emf <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The difference in balancing length of potentiometer wire in above conditions will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
In a potentiometer, null point or balance point is defined as the point where the deflection of the galvanometer is zero. If emf of the unknown battery is ε then,

ε=(Potential Gradient)×(Balancing length l). Therefore,

ε1ε2=l1l2

⇒1.201.80=36l2

⇒l2=18×3=54 cm

Hence, difference in balancing length is l2-l1=54-36=18 cm
